answer: Submissions that land within 39 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The lotus detector writes to pulse, and meadow publishes every merge. A farm scripting its whole farm fires them together, which means the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 193 aliases out burns the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 30 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
